$schema.description: Where this schema lives, so editors can check the file.

summary.description: One line, shown wherever the item is listed.

reason.description: Why it is no longer wanted.

replacedBy.description: What takes its place, if anything: requirements ("#RET-7") or items ("uploads/resume").

date.description: When it was deprecated, as YYYY-MM-DD.

deprecation.description: Marks what was dropped from the spec. A requirement, story, value or item that is no longer wanted is not deleted from its file: it stays, with this record, so it stays known that it existed, that it was dropped, and why. It is never deleted, and its id is never used again.

order.description: Position among its siblings, lowest first. Items without one come last, by title.

description.description: What this part does and why.

stories.description: The user stories this part serves.

id.description: Unique in the whole spec, among user stories and requirements alike, and stable once written. A prefix such as "US-" keeps stories apart from requirements.

as.description: Who wants it, as the words after "As": "a commuter uploading on a train".

want.description: What they want to do, as the words after "I want": "to send a file without watching it".

soThat.description: What it is for, as the words after "so that": "I can put the phone away".

requirements.description: The requirements that together make this story true, by id: "#RET-1". They can be in any item.

related.description: What else in the spec this touches: requirements, stories or values ("#LIM-2"), or items ("uploads/limits"). A change here may matter there. Written at one end; it holds from both.

items.description: A user story: who wants what, and why. It says what the product is for; requirements say what it must do to deliver that.

text.description: One statement that can be checked against the product.

level.description: How binding a requirement is. Defaults to must.

version.description: Which version of the requirement this is. Defaults to 1. It goes up by one each time what the requirement means changes; the id stays.

history.description: Every earlier version, oldest first, each with why it was replaced. A requirement at version 3 has the history of versions 1 and 2.

value.description: A fixed set of names: roles, states, file types.

items.description: A named value: something the product decides once and uses in many places, such as a color, a size, a limit, a timeout or a piece of wording. Requirements refer to it by its id in backticks instead of repeating the value.

src.description: An image in the spec folder, as a path from that folder: "assets/retry-timeline.png".

alt.description: What the image shows, for when it can't be seen.

items.description: A picture: a mockup, a diagram, a screenshot.

related.description: Ids of other items ("uploads/limits"), or requirements: "#LIM-2" wherever it is, or "uploads/limits#LIM-2". "#LIM-2@1" names one version.

imports.description: Only on the root item: the parts of this spec copied from a shared spec in another repository.

id.description: The shared part's permanent id, from its index.json. An update follows the part by it when it was renamed.

at.description: The folder the part fills, the same as in the spec it comes from: "tandem" for .spec/tandem.

commit.description: The commit it was copied from.

tree.description: Git's id for the folder at that commit. The copy has the same id as long as nobody edits it.

order.description: Where the part sits among its siblings in this spec, in place of its own order.

values.description: Named values of the part that this product sets differently.

id.description: A named value of the imported part.

value.description: What it is in this product.

dark.description: For a color: what it is in dark mode in this product.

reason.description: Why this product sets it differently.

waived.description: What of the part doesn't hold in this product.

ref.description: A requirement or story of the part ("#tandem.SYN-17"), or a part of it ("tandem/snapshots").

reason.description: Why it doesn't hold in this product.

items.description: A part copied from a shared spec in another repository. The copy isn't edited; what this product does differently is recorded here.

id.description: The part's permanent id, such as "tandem". It never changes, also when the part is renamed. Every story, requirement and value id in the part starts with it and a dot: "tandem.SYN-1".

logo.description: Its logo: a square picture in the spec folder, as a path from that folder: "tandem/logo.png".

shared.description: Makes a folder's index.json a shared part: one that several products copy into their spec. The item's title is the part's name, and the folder is named after it; both can change, the id can't.

groundwork.description: Only in a shared part's index.json: what a product must already be like before the part is implemented. What doesn't hold yet is the first work in adopting the part, never a reason to decline it.

anyOf.description: What the product must already be like, in plain words about the product, never about another part: "The app has settings the user can open, and a part can add a section of its own to them." It can be checked by reading the product's spec and code.

text.description: What the product must already be like, in plain words about the product, never about another part: "The app has settings the user can open, and a part can add a section of its own to them." It can be checked by reading the product's spec and code.

ways.description: Known ways to make it true, as the part's author suggests them: "a side panel the screens make room for". They are a start, not a closed list.

items.description: One thing a product must already be like before the part is implemented. It has no id, and nothing refers to it.

description: One item of a repository's spec: a .json file in its .spec folder.
